**Simple Self‑Care Plan for a Minor Health Issue** > **Goal:** Give you a quick, self‑guided routine you can follow the next time you notice a small symptom, using the decision framework from the health‑triage checklist and the low‑friction organization habits you already trust. --- ### 1. Capture the “Signal” 1. **Pause & Note (≈30 seconds).** Open your pocket notebook (or phone note) and write: *Date / time, symptom, intensity (1‑10), any triggers.* *(See [[concepts/pocket-notebook-workflow]] and [[concepts/low-friction-organization]])* 2. **Take a quick photo** (if you have a rash, swelling, etc.) and attach it to the note for later reference. --- ### 2. Scan for **Universal Red Flags** Check the list below; if **any** apply, skip to **Step 5** (urgent care). | Red‑Flag | Why it matters | |----------|----------------| | Sudden, severe pain | May indicate a serious underlying problem | | Trouble breathing / chest pain | Possible cardiac/respiratory emergency | | Confusion, fainting, or rapid mental change | Neurologic emergency | | Rapidly worsening symptoms | Could be infection spreading | | Severe dehydration (dark urine, dizziness, very little output) | Needs prompt medical fluids | *(Based on [[concepts/universal-red-flags]])* --- ### 3. Apply **Symptom‑Duration Thresholds** | Symptom | Home‑care window | When to call a doctor | When to seek urgent care/ER | |---------|------------------|-----------------------|------------------------------| | **Fever** | < 102 °F, < 3 days | 102‑103 °F lasting > 3 days | > 103 °F or any fever > 3 days with worsening | | **Vomiting / Diarrhoea** | Improves within 24‑48 h, no blood | > 48 h or any blood | Severe dehydration, persistent vomiting | | **Sore throat** | < 3 days, no white patches | > 3 days *or* white patches, fever, swollen glands → consider [[entities/streptococcal-pharyngitis]] testing | | **Headache** | < 2 days, normal response to OTC | > 2 days or new pattern, worsening, visual changes | | **Back pain / Sciatica** | Improves within 7 days, no numbness | > 7 days or functional loss | New neurological signs, loss of bladder/bowel control | *(All thresholds from [[concepts/symptom-duration-thresholds]] and the checklist in [[summaries/session-14_2024-06-15]])* --- ### 4. Self‑Care Actions (if no red flag & within home‑care window) | Action | How‑to | |--------|--------| | **Rest** | Set a “quiet period” of 30‑60 min; avoid strenuous activity. | | **Hydration** | Aim for ≥ 2 L water / day; sip electrolytes if vomiting or diarrhoea. | | **Temperature control** | Light clothing, cool compress, or a lukewarm shower for fever. | | **OTC Relief** | • Acetaminophen or ibuprofen for pain/fever (follow label).
• Decongestant or cough suppressant for cold/flu symptoms. | | **Nutrition** | Light, easy‑to‑digest meals (broth, toast, bananas). | | **Monitoring** | Re‑check symptom intensity every 4 h; update your notebook entry. | | **Testing (optional)** | If fever + cough or sudden aches → consider rapid test for [[entities/covid-19]] or [[entities/influenza]]. | --- ### 5. Escalation Path (if red flag *or* thresholds crossed) 1. **Urgent care / ER** – Call the nearest urgent‑care centre or go straight to the [[entities/emergency-room]] if red flags are present. 2. **Doctor’s office** – If symptom duration/severity meets the “call a doctor” column, schedule a tele‑visit or in‑person appointment. 3. **Document** – Note the decision, time, and any contact details in your notebook for future reference. --- ### 6. End‑of‑Day Review (5 min) - Look back at today’s entry. - Mark the symptom as **resolved**, **ongoing**, or **escalated**. - If resolved, note what helped the most (e.g., hydration, rest). - If ongoing, plan tomorrow’s next check‑in. *(End‑of‑day habit from [[concepts/end-of-day-scan]])* --- #### Quick Reference Card (keep on your phone) ``` 🔴 Red flags? → ER/urgent care ⏱️ Fever <102°F <3d → rest + fluids ⏱️ Fever 102‑103°F >3d → call doctor ⏱️ Fever >103°F → urgent care 🤒 Sore throat >3d + white patches → strep test 💧 Dehydration signs? → urgent care 📝 Log symptom, re‑check every 4h, adjust care ``` Follow this loop whenever a minor issue pops up. It lets you stay in control, act fast on warning signs, and keep the process low‑friction—exactly the style you’ve found works best for you.
